title: Ensure ESXi host is in Lockdown Mode (Normal or Strict)
description: Lockdown Mode prevents direct access to the ESXi host, requiring all management operations to go through vCenter Server. Normal lockdown permits DCUI access; Strict lockdown does not.
rationale: Enabling Lockdown Mode reduces the attack surface by centralizing access control through vCenter. Local or direct access bypasses vCenter's audit capabilities.
check_content:
Navigate to the ESXi host in vCenter → Configure → Security Profile → Lockdown Mode.
Verify it is set to 'Normal' or 'Strict'.
CLI: vim-cmd -server <host> hostsvc/advopt/view defaultLockdownMode
fix_text:
In vCenter: Select host → Configure → Security Profile → Edit Lockdown Mode → Set to 'Normal' or 'Strict'.
PowerCLI: Get-VMHost <host> | Set-VMHost -State Maintenance; then set lockdown via the vSphere API.

title: Ensure SSH service is disabled on ESXi hosts
description: The SSH service on ESXi should be disabled unless explicitly required for troubleshooting. SSH access bypasses Lockdown Mode controls.
rationale: SSH provides a remote command-line interface that, if left enabled, expands the attack surface. All routine management should be performed through vCenter.
check_content:
In vCenter: Select host → Configure → Services → SSH → Verify Status is 'Stopped' and Startup Policy is 'Start and stop manually' or 'Stop unless started manually'.
ESXi Shell: esxcli system maintenanceMode get (check if SSH running)
fix_text:
In vCenter: Select host → Configure → Services → SSH → Stop the service and set Startup Policy to 'Start and stop manually'.
PowerCLI: Get-VMHostService -VMHost <host> | Where {$_.Key -eq 'TSM-SSH'} | Stop-VMHostService

title: Ensure ESXi Shell (local DCUI) is disabled or restricted
description: The ESXi Shell provides a command-line interface for local management. In production environments, it should be disabled or restricted to prevent unauthorized local access.
rationale: The ESXi Shell bypasses normal access controls and can be used to make changes outside of vCenter's visibility and audit trail.
check_content:
In vCenter: Host → Configure → Services → ESXi Shell → Verify service is stopped.
Check: esxcli system settings advanced list -o /UserVars/ESXiShellInteractiveTimeOut
fix_text:
Disable the ESXi Shell service via vCenter: Host → Configure → Services → ESXi Shell → Stop.
Set timeout: esxcli system settings advanced set -o /UserVars/ESXiShellTimeOut -i 600

title: Ensure NTP is configured and synchronized on ESXi hosts
description: ESXi hosts must synchronize time with authoritative NTP servers to ensure accurate timestamps for logs, certificates, and security events.
rationale: Inaccurate system time can cause authentication failures (Kerberos), invalidate log correlation, and render certificates invalid. It also hampers forensic investigation.
check_content:
In vCenter: Host → Configure → Time Configuration → Verify NTP servers are configured and NTP service is running.
CLI: esxcli system ntp get
fix_text:
In vCenter: Host → Configure → Time Configuration → Edit → Add NTP server IPs → Start NTP service with Startup Policy 'Start and stop with host'.
CLI: esxcli system ntp set --enabled=true --server=<ntp-ip>

title: Ensure ESXi is configured to send logs to a remote syslog server
description: ESXi host logs should be forwarded to a centralized, remote syslog server to preserve audit trails and enable centralized monitoring.
rationale: Local logs on ESXi can be overwritten or destroyed if the host is compromised or fails. Remote logging ensures log integrity and supports security monitoring.
check_content:
CLI: esxcli system syslog config get
Verify 'Remote Host' is set to the syslog server address.
Also check vCenter: Host → Configure → Advanced System Settings → Syslog.global.logHost
fix_text:
Set remote syslog:
esxcli system syslog config set --loghost='udp://<syslog-server>:514'
esxcli system syslog reload
Open firewall: esxcli network firewall ruleset set --ruleset-id=syslog --enabled=true

title: Ensure the Managed Object Browser (MOB) is disabled
description: The Managed Object Browser (MOB) provides an HTTP interface for browsing VMware managed objects. It should be disabled in production environments.
rationale: The MOB exposes sensitive hypervisor information and can be exploited to enumerate configurations. It serves no operational purpose in production.
check_content:
CLI: vim-cmd proxysvc/service_list | grep mob
Or check Advanced Settings: Config.HostAgent.plugins.solo.enableMob = false
fix_text:
Disable via Advanced Settings in vCenter:
Host → Configure → Advanced System Settings → Config.HostAgent.plugins.solo.enableMob → Set to 'false'.
Or: esxcli system settings advanced set -o /Config/HostAgent/plugins/solo/enableMob -s false

title: Ensure ESXi host firewall is configured to restrict access
description: The ESXi host firewall should be configured to allow only necessary services from authorized management networks and block all others.
rationale: Default firewall rules may allow broad access. Restricting access to management networks reduces exposure to unauthorized hosts attempting to manage the hypervisor.
check_content:
CLI: esxcli network firewall ruleset list
For each enabled ruleset, verify allowed IP ranges are set:
esxcli network firewall ruleset allowedip list --ruleset-id=<id>
fix_text:
Restrict access to management services:
esxcli network firewall ruleset set --ruleset-id=sshClient --allowed-all=false
esxcli network firewall ruleset allowedip add --ruleset-id=sshClient --ip-address=<mgmt-network-cidr>

title: Ensure only TLS 1.2 or higher is used for ESXi management
description: ESXi management interfaces should be configured to use only TLS 1.2 or higher, disabling older protocols (SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1).
rationale: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 have known vulnerabilities (POODLE, BEAST). Enforcing TLS 1.2+ ensures encrypted management traffic is protected against protocol downgrade attacks.
check_content:
Check Advanced Settings: UserVars.ESXiVPsDisabledProtocols
Expected value should include 'tlsv1,tlsv1.1,sslv3'.
CLI: esxcli system settings advanced list -o /UserVars/ESXiVPsDisabledProtocols
fix_text:
Set the disabled protocols:
esxcli system settings advanced set -o /UserVars/ESXiVPsDisabledProtocols -s 'tlsv1,tlsv1.1,sslv3'
Restart the hostd service: /etc/init.d/hostd restart

title: Ensure VM disk shrinking and wiping is disabled
description: The ability to shrink or wipe virtual machine disks should be disabled to prevent potential data exposure and denial-of-service conditions.
rationale: Disk wiping operations are I/O intensive and can fill datastore space, causing denial of service. Disabling this prevents VMs from being used to attack the underlying storage.
check_content:
For each VM, check VMX configuration:
grep -i 'isolation.tools.diskWiper.disable\|isolation.tools.diskShrink.disable' <vmname>.vmx
Both should be set to 'TRUE'.
fix_text:
Edit each VM's .vmx file or set via vCenter (VM → Edit Settings → VM Options → Advanced → Configuration Parameters):
isolation.tools.diskWiper.disable = TRUE
isolation.tools.diskShrink.disable = TRUE

title: Ensure VMs are not connected to unauthorized networks (VLAN validation)
description: Virtual machine network adapters should only be connected to VLANs that are explicitly authorized. Validate that no VM uses VLAN 4095 (VLAN trunking) unless required.
rationale: Unauthorized VLAN access could allow a VM to intercept traffic from other network segments, enabling eavesdropping or lateral movement across security zones.
check_content:
In vCenter: Review each port group's VLAN ID.
Verify no port group has VLAN ID 4095 unless trunking is explicitly authorized.
PowerCLI: Get-VirtualPortGroup | Select Name, VLanId
fix_text:
For unauthorized VLANs:
In vCenter: Networking → Port Group → Edit → Change VLAN ID to the authorized VLAN.
Remove VM NICs connected to unauthorized port groups.
